[[File:Annalisa Crannell speaking.jpg|thumb|Annalisa Crannell speaking at Franklin & Marshall College in 2017]]
'''Annalisa Crannell''' is an American mathematician, and an expert in the mathematics of [[water waves]], [[chaos theory]], and [[Perspective (geometry)|geometric perspective]]. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Franklin & Marshall College]].{{r|profile}}

==Education==
Crannell is the daughter of [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] Hall L. Crannell of the [[Catholic University of America]], and [[solar physics|solar physicist]] [[Carol Jo Crannell]] of the [[NASA]] [[Goddard Space Flight Center]].{{r|engle}} As a high school student, her favorite subject was Spanish, and she was indifferent to mathematics.{{r|wim}}

She entered [[Bryn Mawr College]]{{r|cv}} intending to continue her language studies, but was inspired to change majors to mathematics by professor  Mario Martelli, who noted her talent in a calculus class and encouraged her to take a senior-level class in [[partial differential equation]]s as a freshman.{{r|wim}}
She graduated in 1986, with [[Latin honors|magna cum laude honors]],{{r|cv}} and completed her Ph.D. in 1992 from [[Brown University]], with [[Walter Craig (mathematician)|Walter Craig]] as her [[doctoral advisor]].{{r|cv|mgp}}

==Career==
Crannell joined the faculty of [[Franklin & Marshall College]] in 1992.{{r|cv}}
She was the founding Don of Bonchek College House (formerly South Ben College House),{{r|Todd}} serving as don from 2005 to 2010.{{r|Brown}}

She was section governor of the East Pennsylvania Delaware section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (2014-2016), and was a member of the executive committee of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] from 2012 to 2015.{{r|cv}} She has also chaired the Nominating Committee of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2003–2005).{{r|Franklin}}

She has been the associate editor of ''Mathematics Magazine'', published by the Mathematical Association of America (MAA), for over 15 years.{{r|Franklin}}

==Contributions==
{{external media | width = 210px | float = right | headerimage= [[File:Annalisa Crannell interviewed.jpg|210px]]  | audio1 = [https://science360.gov/radio/episode/8891def3-84fb-4c31-bc81-9b6d7da06ff8/mathematics-professor-annalisa-crannell-discusses-course-perspective-use-math-see “Mathematics professor Annalisa Crannell discusses her course on perspective and how to use math to see a work of art as the artist did”], Mathematical Moments, [[American Mathematical Society]]}}

Crannell's dissertation, ''The Existence of Many Non-Traveling, Periodic Solutions of the Boussinesq Equation'', concerned the [[Boussinesq approximation (water waves)|Boussinesq approximation for water waves]].{{r|mgp}}

She is the author or editor of the following books:
*''Starting Our Careers: A Collection of Essays and Advice on Professional Development from the Young Mathematicians' Network'' (edited with Curtis D. Bennett, [[American Mathematical Society]], 1999)
*''Writing Projects for Mathematics Courses: Crushed Clowns, Cars, and Coffee to Go'' (with Gavin LaRose, Thomas Ratliff, and Elyn Rykken, MAA, 2004){{r|clowns}}
*''[[Viewpoints: Mathematical Perspective and Fractal Geometry in Art]]'' (with Marc Frantz, Princeton University Press, 2011){{r|viewpoints}}
*''Perspective and Projective Geometry'' (with Marc Frantz and [[Fumiko Futamura]], Princeton University Press, 2019){{r|perpro}}

Her recent research has included studies of [[Perspective (geometry)|perspective]] in art, such as in the engravings of [[Albrecht Dürer]]. One of her techniques for understanding the perspective of artworks is to bring [[chopsticks]] to art galleries, which she uses as a convenient tool for finding [[vanishing point]]s and, from these points, determining the best points to stand when viewing the art.{{r|lamb}}

==Recognition==
Crannell won the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 2008.<ref name=web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award |archive-date=June 8, 2024 }}</ref> The award recognizes outstanding mathematics teachers "whose teaching effectiveness has been shown to have had influence beyond their own institutions".{{r|haimo}}  

Crannell won the [[Lindback Award|Christian R. And Mary F. Lindback Foundation Award For Distinguished Teaching]] in 2016.{{r|Franklin}}

==Interests==
Crannell ran in her first [[Ironman Triathlon]] on August 24, 2014.{{r|Durantine}}
